title: Why Macro Investing Matters More Than Ever - Kenneth Tropin on Markets, Volatility & Opportunity

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Why Macro Investing Matters More Than Ever - Kenneth Tropin on Markets, Volatility & Opportunity.docx

speakers: Kenneth Tropin (founder and chairman, Graham Capital Management)
summary:
iConnections fireside chat (June 2025) with the founder of Graham Capital, a quant and discretionary macro manager.
Macro demand rises because rates move far more, stocks look expensive, bonds are risky with large deficits, and geopolitics is unstable; macro is uncorrelated rather than reliably negatively correlated.
He favors adding fundamental and carry signals to trend, supervised AI, and warns that a bond-market scare (duration risk) is the key risk.

coverage.note: intro, firm history, culture and employee retention, original clients (no method content)
why macro interest is rising: rate-move frequency, valuations, deficits, geopolitics; macro protective in equity down quarters
macro not always negative to stocks/bonds, tactical long/short flexibility, correlation hit rate, trend following conditions
short-term quant in volatile policy, fundamentals plus price, trend additivity, 2022, AI and research, quant plus discretionary
discretionary scalability, Fed watching, multi-strat comparison and sleeves
team correlation and time horizons, crowding balance, policy chaos outlook
Fed, new chair, duration risk and bond market canary, 1980 analogy, charity

completeness_estimate: 0.88 - first reader captured all macro and quant content (rate-move counts, correlation profile, signal blending, AI use, duration risk); missed organizational and structure remarks (pod vs collaborative teams, custom solutions, crowding in team correlation) and client demand data. C01 was left with no claims and is mostly culture.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: There were only 13, 25 basis point rate moves between those three central banks and 11 years and in the subsequent 36 months there have been 60.
claims.claim: Fed, ECB and BoE made only 13 quarter-point moves in the 11 years to 2021 versus 60 in the following 36 months, so fixed-income trading opportunity is about 20 times larger.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: And so we're in an environment where stocks are really expensive and bonds are kind of scary.
claims.claim: Record equity valuations, unstable geopolitics and record deficits make both stocks and bonds risky, so macro is attractive as an asset uncorrelated to stocks and bonds.

claims.speaker: Moderator
claims.quote: looking at quarters when equities were down, macro typically protects and sometimes even actually up substantially when, you know, equities are down.
claims.claim: Since the GFC, macro funds typically protected or gained in quarters when equities fell.
claims.indicator: macro index vs equity down quarters

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: We don't always make money when it's bad for stocks and bonds.
claims.claim: Macro funds did well in some bad periods (2008, 1987, 2003 tech bust) but cannot promise to, since they can be long equities when they fall.
claims.indicator: macro fund returns in equity/bond drawdowns

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: we can switch from being long equities to short equities
claims.claim: Tactical long/short flexibility plus trading FX and commodities that are uncorrelated to equities makes macro diversifying.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: we hope to be negatively correlated when clients need us most. We have about two thirds of three quarters of the time.
claims.claim: Macro aims to be uncorrelated rather than negatively correlated; it was negatively correlated to stocks in about two thirds to three quarters of the bad periods.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: If they're trends, usually you're doing pretty well. If there are a lack of trends, probably not.
claims.claim: Trend following uses momentum signals and does well when trends exist, poorly when trends are absent or reverse.
claims.conditions: fails with lack of trends or reversals; recent weeks of policy volatility were tough

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: there's just no way to be successful over time if you're not always pushing the boundaries of innovation
claims.claim: Alpha decays, so sustaining performance requires continually innovating.

correction.issue: Tropin does not say that alpha decays; he says a manager must always look around the corner for the next source of alpha and keep pushing the boundaries of innovation (the quote is also garbled in the captions). The decay mechanism is the first reader's inference.
correction.fix: Sustaining performance in hedge fund investing, including quant, requires always looking for the next source of alpha and continually pushing the boundaries of innovation.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: tactical and short term in nature, they can do a lot better in this kind of an environment
claims.claim: During the volatile, rapidly changing 2025 tariff policy environment, medium-term quant strategies struggle while high-frequency and short-term tactical strategies do better.
claims.testable: yes - compare horizons in the period

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: quant strategies that are not just based on price, but also that are based on fundamentals, things that look at, yield and carry, relative value, all of these things are complementary
claims.claim: Quant strategies using fundamentals such as yield, carry and relative value are complementary to price-based trend if the architecture is well done.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: it's additive, right? I mean, at the end of the day, people love trend followers.
claims.claim: Adding non-correlated alpha sources to trend following improves the information ratio and is a firm priority.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: In a year like 22, when we really performed at a time where very little else worked
claims.claim: Trend/macro performed in 2022 when little else worked, which makes trend followers valued.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: every cycle that hasn't been good for what we do, to me has been a catalyst to say, roll up our sleeves
claims.claim: Each poor period is used as a catalyst to improve the models for that market character.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: you can really expedite research and how fast we can test different ideas
claims.claim: AI tools accelerate research and idea testing.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: What we don't necessarily have a lot of confidence in at this time is just asking the computers to design, trading systems.
claims.claim: AI-designed trading systems are not trusted; the process must be closely supervised.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: can just doing quant, you know, it's going to be to hit or miss. You should diversify into discretionary
claims.claim: Graham added discretionary trading in 1998 because quant alone was hit or miss; blending quant and discretionary diversifies.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: nature, relying on people and not machines is harder to scale
claims.claim: Discretionary macro relies on people and is harder to scale than quant.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: when monetary policy was on hold. And he said, Ken, there's just nothing for me to do.
claims.claim: Fed-watching alpha disappears when monetary policy is on hold; edge depends on policy activity.
claims.conditions: when the Fed is on hold

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: you might have a 20% sleeve a macro within their big fund. But if you want to specifically allocate to a macro that's not happening.
claims.claim: Large multi-strategy funds hold only a small macro sleeve, so they cannot substitute for a dedicated macro allocation.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: it used to be on average 10%, which is pretty low
claims.claim: Graham's discretionary teams averaged about 10% pairwise correlation, higher in turbulent periods; different time horizons keep correlation low.
claims.conditions: higher when much is going on and positions are crowded

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: there's a balancing or an equilibrium between being in the moves that matter but not being so concentrated
claims.claim: Balance participating in big moves (gold, Bitcoin, weak dollar) with avoiding concentration.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: I think it's just going to contract in terms of what's happening in terms of the spontaneity of it all.
claims.claim: Policy chaos (tariff announce-and-postpone) should calm toward the midterms, making it easier for models to capture moves that ultimately prevail.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: The fed, right, knows that these tariffs are inflationary. So they can't really be as dovish as they'd like to be.
claims.claim: Tariffs are inflationary, so the Fed cannot be as dovish as it would like; a likely new hawkish chair (Warsh) adds to this.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: for, 25 years, there's been no premium for taking duration, risk.
claims.claim: There has been no term premium for duration risk for 25 years, which leaves holders exposed if yields rise.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: in 1980, interest rates went from something like 6 or 8% to 20 people got killed in duration, risk and bonds
claims.claim: Analogy: in 1980 rates jumped from 6-8% to 20%, hurting bondholders; the same risk now arises with large deficits.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: to me, that the canary in the room to watch is, is the bond market.
claims.claim: The key risk is investors getting spooked by bonds in a way not seen in a long time, hitting both fixed income and equities.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: The way I look at having a successful hedge fund, it's all about having the best possible people.
claims.claim: A manager's edge rests on hiring and keeping the best people, which requires investing in their careers and well-being and a culture of collaboration; Graham shows 40% of 235 staff with over ten years of tenure and its first five clients still invested after 30 years.

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: we probably have 3 or 4 times as many client meetings, in the last couple of years than say, we might have had five years ago
claims.claim: Allocator demand for macro has risen sharply (3 to 4 times as many client meetings as five years ago), a sign that investors are shifting toward macro as the stock-bond mix looks fragile.
claims.conditions: high rate volatility, stretched equity valuations and uncertain bond hedge
claims.testable: partly - flows into macro funds can be checked against HFR or SG indices

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: work with clients in a partnership fashion to give them a very custom investment solution, rather than a one size fits all fund
claims.claim: Instead of copying multi-strategy platforms, a dedicated macro manager can compete by building custom exposure for each client (discretionary or quant blend, leverage level, volatility target), which gives the allocator a specific macro exposure that a multi-strat sleeve cannot.
claims.conditions: allocators wanting a specific macro exposure

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: You're given capital, you're given risk limits and maybe not even encouraged to collaborate because they're really striving to have the lowest correlation between the portfolio teams as possible.
claims.claim: Multi-strategy pod platforms give each team capital and risk limits and discourage collaboration to keep the correlation between portfolio teams as low as possible, whereas Graham deliberately encourages collaboration while still keeping low team correlation.
claims.testable: partly - team-level return correlations can be compared across structures

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: there's more going on that's pretty significant. And people you know are going to we're going to have some crowded positions.
claims.claim: When major macro events dominate, separate discretionary teams converge on the same trades, so team correlation rises and positions become crowded; teams with very different time horizons are the main offset.
claims.conditions: big macro moves in gold, Bitcoin or the dollar
claims.testable: yes - team or manager correlation rises with event intensity

claims.speaker: Kenneth Tropin
claims.quote: I think it was a big goal for Trump to try and be the peacemaker in, in Eastern Europe and in the Mideast didn't happen. And so, these things are going to stay relevant for for a while.
claims.claim: Because the attempt to broker peace in Eastern Europe and the Middle East has not succeeded, geopolitical conflict will stay relevant to markets for some time, supporting a lasting role for macro trading.
